works.title: The World Without Humans
works.author: KapiTomo
works.summary: At 14, Caio wakes up in a world without humans, where dragons, goblins, and elves attack any stranger. To return alive, he must learn to survive without pretending to be a hero.

chapters.title: Chapter 01 - The Fall
chapters.text:
Caio was fourteen and walking home from school when the ground disappeared. One second earlier there had been asphalt, a heavy backpack, and the noise of buses. The next, there was mud up to his ankles, cold air, and a forest that breathed like a huge animal.

He called for someone. Nobody answered. There were no poles, houses, cars, or human voices. Only trees that were too tall, dark leaves, and claw marks on the trunks. Caio tightened the strap of his backpack and tried not to cry.

A roar tore through the sky. Between the clouds, a winged shadow drifted slowly past. It was a dragon. Not a drawing, not a dream. A real dragon, as large as a building, searching the valley for something.

Caio ran under a giant root and held his breath. The monster landed far away, but the wind from its wings knocked branches down around him. When everything went quiet, he opened his backpack. He had one bottle of water, two loaves of bread, a notebook, a small flashlight, and a simple pocketknife he used to sharpen pencils.

It was not much. But it was everything. Caio decided he would not waste energy screaming. First he needed shelter. Then water. Then a way to understand where he was.

While walking, he found small footprints near a stream. He thought they belonged to a child until he saw an arrow stuck in a stone. Its tip was stained with green poison.

Thin laughter rose from the bushes. Goblins. Four of them, short, skinny, and armed with curved knives, surrounded the stream while sniffing the air. Caio threw himself into the mud behind a rock and covered his mouth with his sleeve.

One goblin passed so close that Caio saw its broken teeth and yellow eyes. If he moved, he would die right there. So he stayed still, counting the beats of his own heart.

When the goblins left, Caio understood the first rule of that world: everything there saw a human as food, an enemy, or something too strange to leave alive. He picked up the poisoned arrow carefully, buried the fear deep in his chest, and kept walking before night arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 02 - The Hunting Forest
chapters.text:
Caio spent the first night inside the hollow trunk of a tree. He did not truly sleep. Every crack sounded like a step, every shadow like a claw. When the gray sun rose, he was hungry, cold, and covered in mud.

He ate half a loaf of bread and saved the rest. In his notebook, he wrote three rules: do not run without knowing where to go, do not make fire during the day, and do not trust anyone armed.

The third rule failed before noon. Near a clearing, Caio saw two elves. They were tall, beautiful, and silent, with long bows and pale leather clothes. For one second, he almost asked for help.

Then he saw what they were doing. The elves were chasing a small wounded creature, laughing whenever it stumbled. One of them shot an arrow just to cut off the victim's path. They were not hunting for food. They were playing.

Caio stepped back slowly, but his foot snapped a branch. Both elves turned their faces at the same time. Their eyes were silver and cold. One of them smiled like someone finding a new toy.

Caio ran. He remembered his own rule too late. Arrows hissed past his ears. He entered a part of the woods where the trees had red thorns and threw himself beneath them. The elves hesitated. The thorns moved on their own.

With the pocketknife, Caio cut strips from his own shirt and wrapped them around his arms so he could cross the brush without tearing his skin. An arrow struck his backpack but stayed caught in the fabric. He did not look back.

At the end of the trail, he found a low cave. Inside there were old bones and the smell of an animal, but there were also dry stones. Caio entered, pulled branches over the opening, and waited.

When night fell, the elves gave up. Caio was shaking all over. Even so, he did something important: he broke the arrow stuck in his backpack and kept the tip. In that world, any tool could become a chance.

He was not strong. He did not know how to fight. But he knew how to observe. And if he could survive one more day, maybe he would discover a way out.

chapters.title: Chapter 03 - The Stone Exit
chapters.text:
The next morning, Caio found old marks on the wall of the cave. They were not drawings of animals. They were arrows, circles, and a symbol repeated three times: a door inside a mountain.

He followed the marks through a narrow tunnel. The flashlight failed twice, and the darkness seemed to press against his face. When he came out on the other side, he saw stone ruins swallowed by roots. In the center stood a broken arch, just like the symbol on the wall.

The problem was the dragon. It slept curled around the ruins, smoke leaking from its nose. Between its scales were scars from spears and arrows. Even the elves and goblins feared it.

Caio hid and thought. He could not fight. He could not run. So he did the only thing he still knew how to do better than the monsters: improvise.

He used the empty bottle, small stones, and the arrow tip to make a rattle. He tied everything to a vine and threw it far away against a fallen column. The noise echoed through the ruin.

The dragon opened one eye. Then the other. It raised its head and moved toward the sound, irritated. Caio ran low, almost crawling, toward the stone arch.

The portal did not light up. Something was missing. Caio saw a hole in the center of the base, exactly the size of the flashlight. He swallowed hard, placed the object there, and pressed the button.

The weak light became a white line. The whole arch trembled. The dragon noticed and roared. Caio felt heat reaching his back, but he did not take his hand off the flashlight.

When the portal opened, he saw for one instant the street near his home. The same pole, the same tagged wall, the same loud human world that had once seemed too ordinary.

Caio jumped. He landed on the asphalt on his knees, with his backpack torn and mud up to his neck. The portal closed behind him like a sigh.

Nobody would believe him. Maybe even he would stop believing after a few days. But inside his backpack, there was still a black scale, hot as an ember.

Caio put the scale in his pocket and looked at the sky. He was home. But now he knew one thing he would never forget: surviving was not defeating every monster. It was continuing to think when fear wanted to think for him.
